problem: The first trap is written as a flat statement of fact — 'A name typed at the prompt is still there tomorrow' — which is false and directly contradicts Section 2. Every other trap in the list is phrased as a mistake the student makes, so this one reads like a rule to memorise.
fix: Phrase it as the mistake: 'Expecting a name typed at the prompt to still be there tomorrow. A new session starts with an empty namespace; only a saved script repeats the steps.'

problem: 'A line below a failed line may not run' is vaguer than the truth. When a script hits a runtime error, execution stops there and every line below it does not run at all.
fix: Write: 'Forgetting that a script runs top to bottom. When a line fails, execution stops and the lines below it do not run; read the reported line number first, then see 1.8.'
